problem:
The position vector $r$ of a particle $P$ (relative to a fixed origin $O$) at time $t$ is given by

$$
r=⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡({t}^{2}-1),4t-1⟩,\,t>0.
$$

Calculate the velocity vector $v.$

activity_context.topic_title: Calculating Velocity for Plane Motion Using Differentiation

examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Velocity Vector of a Particle Moving in Two Dimensions
examples.problem:
The position vector $\mathbf{r}$ of a particle $P$ relative to a fixed origin $O$ at time $t > 0$ is given by

$$
\mathbf{r} = \langle 3t^3, 2t^2\rangle.
$$

Calculate the velocity vector $\mathbf{v}.$
examples.worked_solution:
The particle's velocity vector is given by the derivative of its position vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3{t}^{3}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{t}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨9{t}^{2},\,4t⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
